segments.content:
Chapter 236 0233 The Mettle of a Keyboard Warrior from Twenty Years Later

Very few tickets were available for Annan's speech this time.

The tickets for the Yuanpei Program were secured by Director Zhu; from freshman to senior year, there were only four in total.

Other departments didn't even have a chance to enter the lottery. The tickets were mainly distributed to student union cadres and top students from the School of International Studies, as well as students who had participated in the "Peking University Model United Nations Conference."

"Ding-a-ling-ling!"

Near the Centennial Hall's bicycle parking area, a senior with a bob haircut was listening to an English cassette tape with her headphones on.

When the bicycle bell rang, she took off her headphones, stood up, and extended her hand with an air of easy grace. "Hello, I'm Zhou Yang."

This senior, Zhou Yang, was from Peking University's School of Foreign Languages.

Although Peking University didn't have a simultaneous interpretation major, graduate students could choose an advanced interpretation course that included a simultaneous interpretation module. Currently, Peking University was also preparing to build a simultaneous interpretation classroom.

"Hello, thank you for your trouble today," Chen Guiliang said.

Zhou Yang smiled. "It's good practice for me."

While locking his bike, Chen Guiliang asked, "Senior, are you planning to become a diplomat in the future?"

Zhou Yang said, "After we graduate with our master's, if we want to get into diplomacy, it's usually through the national civil service exam or a selection process to enter the Foreign Ministry's Department of Translation and Interpretation or the foreign affairs departments of other ministries. The main work is high-level interpretation and written translation."

"That's very impressive, bringing glory to the country," Chen Guiliang said.

The two chatted as they walked into the Centennial Auditorium, where many students and faculty had already gathered.

Once inside, Chen Guiliang quickly struck up a conversation with the students, the topic being entirely about the global situation. Chen Guiliang was mainly responsible for listening, while the other students were responsible for bullshitting.

When he heard absurd arguments, Chen Guiliang couldn't be bothered to debate them.

Around ten in the morning, President Xu escorted the group in.

Besides UN Secretary-General Annan and his wife, there were also the Senior Advisor to the UN Secretary-General, the UNDP Resident Representative in China, a former UN Under-Secretary-General, and China's Ambassador to the United Nations, among others.

First, President Xu gave a speech, heaping praise on Annan and also taking the opportunity to boast about Peking University.

The Dean of Peking University's School of International Studies served as today's host.

Finally, it was Annan's turn to speak. He opened his mouth with a Chinese phrase: "Da-jia-hao!"

The entire audience burst into laughter, accompanied by applause.

Senior Zhou Yang's simultaneous interpretation skills were clearly subpar. She did well at the beginning, but gradually started to struggle.

Often, Annan would finish speaking, and only then would she hastily summarize the meaning and translate it into Chinese.

"He said that the Peking University students present here are China's future builders and leaders, and they will play a crucial role in China's future..."

"He said the biggest challenge your generation faces is ensuring that globalization becomes a positive force. A force that benefits not just a privileged few, but all of humanity."

"He said pandemics, environmental degradation, nuclear proliferation, and terrorism are challenges for all of us..."

"He said... uhm, scientific innovation, information technology, and economic integration can benefit all of us... now he's talking about the Six-Party Talks on the North Korean nuclear issue..."

Halfway through the translation, sweat was already beading on Senior Zhou Yang's forehead.

She very much wanted to do simultaneous interpretation, but her head was buzzing, and in the end, it turned completely into consecutive interpretation.

A failure in practice!

Annan's speech was not long, ending in just over ten minutes.

Chen Guiliang smiled and comforted her, "Don't be nervous."

Zhou Yang sighed, "Sigh, I don't know why I was so nervous. It might be because of who the speaker is."

Next was a Q&A session with the students and faculty, with Annan providing the answers.

Zhou Yang said, "This student is asking, today the world and the UN face many conflicts and contradictions. How should the UN resolve these contradictions."

"Annan's answer is a call for the majority groups in society to be able to express their opinions, rather than letting the opinions of a few dominate society. Uhm, in this process, the basic human rights of people still need to be protected... Huh? Why does that seem to be an irrelevant answer?"

It was indeed an irrelevant answer. Chen Guiliang even suspected that his senior might have translated it incorrectly.

What on earth was this UN Secretary-General rambling about?

The next student raised the issue of environmental protection.

Zhou Yang said, "Annan is recalling his experience planting trees with his wife in Nairobi... I can't be bothered to translate the details, but basically, he's talking about how he planted trees... Here we go. He encourages Peking University students not to give up on individual action just because environmental issues are a big problem. They should contribute to protecting the world's environment within their capabilities."

Another student was chosen, this time asking how to achieve world peace.

Most of the questioners were top students from Peking University's School of International Studies, but the questions they asked were progressively broader and more grandiose.

Asking them was the same as not asking at all!

Chen Guiliang was a bit disappointed by the performance of both the UN Secretary-General and the Peking University students.

He had expected to see a brilliant exchange today.

Finally, something brilliant arrived.

A Peking University student said, "The one-vote veto system in the UN Security Council leads to superpowers like the United States manipulating the UN. Can the one-vote veto system be reformed to uphold the principles of fairness and equality, and to pay attention to the demands and voices of developing countries and small to medium-sized countries?"

Chen Guiliang looked like he had seen a ghost. "This senior, did he really ask that?"

Zhou Yang said, "I didn't mistranslate. Mr. Annan said that he greatly appreciates the role of young students around the world in the issue of globalization. He also stated that he would consider the suggestion to reform the one-vote veto system."

Chen Guiliang really couldn't take it anymore. He immediately stood up and said, "Give me the microphone!"

Up until this point, everyone in the auditorium had been communicating in English. Chen Guiliang's Mandarin sentence was very conspicuous, instantly drawing the attention of everyone present.

The Dean of the School of International Studies, serving as the host, said, "Give him the microphone."

Chen Guiliang took the microphone. "Mr. Annan, I think your previous answer was very perfunctory."

Senior Zhou Yang froze on the spot.

Chen Guiliang urged, "Translate."

"Oh." Zhou Yang quickly translated.

Annan asked, "Why do you say that?"

Chen Guiliang said, "You know perfectly well that the one-vote veto system is impossible to change, yet you say you will consider the suggestion. What is that if not perfunctory? The veto power is the very foundation of the United Nations' existence. If it's gone, the UN will have to disband. May I ask, Mr. Annan, how do you plan to reform it? Are you planning to disband the United Nations?"

Before Annan could answer, the student who had asked the question couldn't help but retort, and he spoke to Chen Guiliang in Mandarin, "How could the foundation of the United Nations possibly be the veto power?"

"Then what do you think it is?" Chen Guiliang retorted.

The student said, "The United Nations is a place where all countries and regions in the world sit together to negotiate and resolve major international issues. The foundation of the United Nations' existence is all of humanity's desire for peace and equality."

Chen Guiliang suddenly realized that this was not yet the era of the information explosion.

Although the other student's words were naive, they represented the consensus of many people at the time.

Even though the US repeatedly trampled on the authority of the UN, people still believed that the UN could resolve major international issues.

As a seasoned political keyboard warrior from 20 years in the future, the common knowledge in Chen Guiliang's mind seemed enough to crush many of his countrymen of the current era.

Chen Guiliang asked, "Do you know about the League of Nations?"

The student said, "Of course I do."

Chen Guiliang said, "A United Nations without veto power, even if it doesn't disband, will become a second League of Nations. If the veto power is abolished, the United States will absolutely withdraw from the UN. Think about it carefully, can a United Nations without the United States still be called the United Nations?"

"The United States will not withdraw," the student said.

Chen Guiliang smiled. "The blood and sweat of so many predecessors were exchanged for China's position in the United Nations. And now you want to throw that position away? I know you feel that China is always being bullied, but is the reason China is bullied America's veto power? Have you forgotten that China has that thing too?"

All the students and faculty in the hall were watching the two of them.

Annan, however, looked completely baffled. He couldn't understand Chinese, and no one was translating for him.

Chen Guiliang continued, "The United Nations exists because of the five permanent members. It's not that the United Nations existed first, and then the five permanent members were chosen. The foundation of the UN's existence is not humanity's desire for peace, but... forget it, it's not appropriate to say such things in public."

On an occasion like this, it really wasn't convenient to speak so plainly.

The student was about to retort again, but the Dean of the School of International Studies said, "Next question. The young man in the blue shirt in the second row, you've had your hand up for a long time. You can ask."

The on-site exchange continued as if nothing had just happened.

Senior Zhou Yang whispered, "You're so bold, to actually challenge the UN Secretary-General on the spot."

Chen Guiliang smiled. "It's nothing."

Although he could understand the cognitive deficiencies brought about by the limitations of the era, he still couldn't stand a Peking University student saying something like that.

He just hoped that the student who suggested abolishing the veto power wasn't from Peking University's School of International Studies. Otherwise, that would be too ridiculous.

After finally making it through the Q&A session, Chen Guiliang immediately bailed.

But the event on site was still going on. President Xu presented a tea set to Annan. The students, for their part, presented dozens of written suggestions to Annan, hoping the UN would adopt them.

Everyone took photos with each other, and the atmosphere was very harmonious and congenial.

"You're back so early?"

His roommate, Tong Zhihong, was playing *World of Warcraft*.

Chen Guiliang said, "The speech wasn't long."

Tong Zhihong asked, "Was Annan's speech super awesome?"

Chen Guiliang said, "It was alright. Where are the other two?"

Tong Zhihong said, "Jiang Junlai is in the study room with his girlfriend. Li Heng went to a student union activity." With that, he turned on his mic, "Hello, hello, can you hear me? Why isn't the guild leader online yet?"

"The guild leader had something urgent come up. I'll be leading in his place today."

"OK, can someone give me a summon?"

Chen Guiliang opened his computer, took out the historical materials he had collected earlier, and started typing away at *Those Things of the Ming Dynasty*.

Tong Zhihong quickly turned down the volume on his speakers. "I'm not bothering you, am I?"

"Not at all. Raiding is more important," Chen Guiliang said with a smile.

Tong Zhihong chuckled and laughed along.

These guys were actually running a raid near noon and had even managed to gather a full team.

More proactive than going to work or class!

After typing for over half an hour, Chen Guiliang was about to go for lunch when he noticed that Tong Zhihong's raid wasn't over yet.

Chen Guiliang couldn't help but log in to the Peking University BBS and, sure enough, found a post about him calling someone out in the morning.

The thread was quite lively.

Below the first few posts, a student replied: "Which department is that dude from? Suggesting the abolition of the veto power is just hilarious."

"Definitely from the School of Foreign Languages. Most of the students who went to the lecture today were from the School of International Studies and the School of Foreign Languages. I don't believe a student from International Studies would say something like that."

"Did this student from the School of Foreign Languages study foreign languages until he went dumb?"

"Chen Zong should have retorted in English, so Annan could hear it properly too."

"Haha, is it possible that Chen Zong only knows how to do 'mute English'? He brought a senior from the School of Foreign Languages as a translator today."

"Bringing a translator is pretty ridiculous too. What are his usual English scores?"

"I'm in the Yuanpei Program. All I know is that Chen Zong hasn't even passed his CET-4 yet."

"Looking forward to the day Chen Zong can't get his diploma."

As Chen Guiliang browsed the thread, he soon noticed something was off. How had the topic derailed to his English proficiency?

These bastards!

There was another thread, however, posted by a graduate student from the School of International Studies, seriously discussing the content of Chen Guiliang's speech.

Namely, if the veto power were abolished, would the United States withdraw from the United Nations.

(End of this chapter)
